newsitem.title: CANADA: Intense snow storm warning for Manitoba Red River.
newsitem.headline: Intense snow storm warning for Manitoba Red River.

text.p: An intense snow storm warning was issued Friday morning for Winnipeg and southeastern Manitoba which may dump up to 20 cms (7.9 inches) of snow on the Red River Valley, a Environment Canada meteorologist said.
"There's always a chance it might miss us but all indications are this will be our last little breath of winter," meteorologist Steve Smith said.

Southeast Manitoba should see between 10 to 20 cms of snow between late Friday night and Saturday morning with winds gusting up to 70 km/h (45 mph) as a low pressure system from Colorado hits a hot, moist air mass from the Gulf, Smith said.
Twelve cms (4.7 inches) of snow remained standing on the ground at Winnipeg International Airport Thursday compared to 43 cms (17 inches) on April 3, 1996, Environment Canada said.
Weekend precipitation could determine the severity of Red River Valley flooding, a Manitoba Natural Resources official said on Thursday.

"We're waiting for this Colorado low (pressure system) that's supposed to dump snow and rain on us this weekend and depending on how much we get, all the favourable weather we've had in the last 10 days may be for naught," MNR's manager of Water Planning and Development Larry Whitney said.
The Red River Valley has seen normal seasonal temperatures in the past week and a half. Thursday noon hour temperature was also at the seasonal normal of 3 Celsius (37.40F).
MNR's last forecast for the Red River Valley set the flood level at one to 1-1/2 feet higher than last year's flood, based on normal spring weather.
Rapid melt or heavy spring rain could see levels three to five feet higher than 1996 between the U.S. border and here.
Last year's flood delayed spring seeding of wheat, barley, canola, flax and corn by one month.
